title: Clarinet players Sidney Bechet and Green, and Baton Rouge musicians
summary: He wished to play against Bechet, recalls Green in Baton Rouge, and Titten Knox's strictly musical band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well that was all that was playing around here at that time. I didn't give up clarinet. When I wanted to, one man I wanted to meet with clarinet was Sidney Bessier. Uh huh. But I never got a chance to play against Sidney because he was in New York. He left a week before I come here. I never got a chance to even hear him play, but on records that's all. But I sure wanted to play against Sidney. He said, when I went to Baton Rouge, I met a fella up there called Green. He had Baton Rouge sewed up in clarinet. Man, that cat would play some clarinet. But after I was up there about six months, he was just another clarinet man.

Who was that guy in Baton Rouge that didn't have any keys on his clarinet? Did you know him? No. That was strange. That's how he could play. Any number you wanted, but he just fingered the holes was all. Stopped everything else up, just used those three fingers on each hand.

I don't know who that was. It beats me. I don't know how he did it. Unless it was Green. They had some nice clarinet players up there now. They were strictly musicians. They couldn't get off at all. Just played strictly music. I had a fella up there by the name of Titten Knox had a band up there. They were fine musicians as well. They were arranging and played that stuff. They sounded good. They really sounded good. But they played strictly about their music. They kept pretty busy too.
